content.title: Comcast Is Paying Up to $10,000 to People Affected by a Data Breach. Here's How to Claim Your Share
content.text: Comcast agreed to pay $117.5 million to customers whose sensitive information was leaked in a data breach. Photo: Adobe StockListen to this ArticleMore info0:00 / 3:49Comcast is finally gearing up to pay for a 2023 hack that leaked sensitive customer information.Comcast disclosed in December 2023 that hackers accessed account usernames and passwords, as well as names, contact information, dates of birth, security questions, and partial social security numbers for some customers. Bad actors took advantage of a vulnerability in software Comcast uses from cloud computing firm Citrix, according to the Associated Press. A portal for payments has gone live, although compensation likely won’t be available until July or later.A class action lawsuit, filed against Comcast on behalf of 36 million Xfinity customers, sought damages related to time and money that people spent in an effort to protect their identities after the leak. They alleged that Comcast did not have adequate cybersecurity mechanisms in place to protect customer data and failed to adequately notify affected customers, according to WGN Chicago. Comcast was not required to admit blame, per the settlement terms, but has agreed to pay $117.5 million to customers affected by the breach. The payments, however, hinge on a final approval hearing, currently scheduled for July 7. Customers have until June 1 to opt-out of payment, or until August 14 to opt-in.Here’s how to get your cut if you think you’ve been affected:Determine your eligibilityOnly customers whose data was compromised can claim payment. Eligible customers have to live in the U.S. or its territories, and have to have used Comcast services during the time of the hack, which was a stretch of about three days in late October 2023, according to a notice from Comcast. Customers also would have had to receive communication from Comcast that their personal data was acquired by bad actors, as well as a Class Member ID. If you didn’t receive a notice from Comcast or misplaced your identification number, you can also search on the settlement website for your Class Member ID, using your name and the email address, phone number, or address, associated with your account.
